Voting information for the November 3 Election

Piedmont Post · October 7, 2026 · 2 min read

On November 3, Piedmont voters will elect representatives to fill three seats on the Piedmont City Council and to federal, state, county, and special district offices. The ballot also includes a proposed increase to the City’s Real Estate Transfer Tax and 14 statewide ballot measures.

All registered Alameda County voters will receive a vote-by-mail ballot. The Registrar of Voters began mailing voter information guides on September 24 and will begin mailing ballots starting Monday, October 5. Sign up for the Registrar of Voters’ Track My Ballot tool to get notified when your ballot is mailed, received, and counted.

The last day to register to vote for the November 3 election is Monday, October 19. If you’re already registered, check your registration status before October 19 to confirm that your information is correct. You’ll need to re-register if you have moved, changed your name, or wish to change your political party preference. Voter registration forms are available at the City Clerk’s Office and from the Registrar of Voters. You can also register to vote online at registertovote. ca.gov.

In Piedmont, ballot drop boxes are near the mailboxes at Highland Way and Mountain Avenue and are available 24 hours a day. The Alameda County Sheriff’s Office picks up ballots from the drop boxes and returns them to the Registrar of Voters daily. The last pickup will be at 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3.

The Registrar of Voters is hosting a series of pop-up events throughout Alameda County where voters can hand their ballot directly to ROV staff. More information on the location of the pop-up events can be found online at: https://acvote.ala-medacountyca.gov/dropstop.

If you mail your ballot through the post office, it must be postmarked by November 3 and received by November 10. Whether submitting your ballot by mail or a secure drop box, remember to sign the back of your return envelope – otherwise your vote will not be counted!

Alameda County voters can vote in person at any of 100 Vote Centers across the county. In Piedmont, the Veterans Memorial Building at 401 Highland Avenue will serve as a Vote Center. All vote centers will be open:

  • Saturday, October 31 – Monday, November 2: 9 a.m. - 5 p.m.
  • Tuesday, November 3: 7 a.m. - 8 p.m. A smaller subset of vote centers will be open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. for 11 days before the election, starting on October 24. The closest 11-day vote center to Piedmont is in Oakland at Parks Chapel AME Church, 476 34th Street.

If you have any questions regarding your voter registration, ballot status, or voting locations, contact the Alameda County Registrar of Voters at (510) 272-6933.
